newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops wound 35 Arabs in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops wound 35 Arabs in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli soldiers shot and wounded at least 35 Palestinians on Tuesday in another flareup of violence over posters depicting the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig, witnesses said.
Two Israeli soldiers were wounded, one of them severely, in an explosion outside a Jewish settler compound in the divided West Bank city, the witnesses said.

A home-made bomb hurled by Palestinians rolled to the feet of Israeli soldiers as they aimed their guns at protesters. A television cameraman recorded the explosion on video-tape followed by scenes of the soldiers on the ground writhing in pain.

Dozens of Arab youths broke away from a peaceful protest which Palestinian dignitaries called in response to the discovery of the crudely drawn posters and threw rocks and petrol bombs at soldiers and settlers.
The dignitaries distributed leaflets during the protest calling for the "shedding of the blood of those responsible for this condemned crime" and the eviction of settlers from Hebron.

Soldiers holed up behind street corners or on rooftops responded by firing rubber-coated metal bullets. Medics at a makeshift field hospital set up in a petrol station courtyard said they treated 35 people for light injuries.

Israeli police on Saturday arrested a 25-year-old Jewish woman from Jerusalem on suspicion of pasting the posters on about 20 storefronts in Hebron. She also had thrown a rock through the windshield of an Arab car, police said.

Palestinian lawmakers meeting in the West Bank town of Ramallah called for a one-hour strike on Wednesday beginning at 12 p.m. (0900 GMT) to protest the posters and what they said was violence directed at Palestinians in Hebron.
Tensions have been fuelled by a freeze in Israeli-PLO peace talks over Israel's groundbreaking for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Palestinians in Hebron were enraged when they discovered the posters of a pig donning an Arab headdress with the word Mohammad written on it in Arabic and English.
The drawing depicted the pig stomping with one foot on the Moslem holy book, the Koran, while holding a pen in the other. Islam and Judaism regard pigs as unclean and ban pork eating.

"Only a sick mind could draw a connection between a pig, the Koran and Mohammad," Jerusalem District Court Judge Ezra Kama said on Tuesday, rejecting an appeal by the suspect, Tatiana Susskind, to be released from police custody.
Susskind told reporters at the court building that police had coerced her into confessing.
Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the poster.
"The only apology that we would accept is to withdraw the settlers from the heart of Hebron," said Rafiq al-Natsheh, a member of the Palestinian Legislative Council, during the demonstration.
Jewish settlers, who number about 400, remained in Hebron guarded by Israeli troops when Israel handed most of the city to Palestinian self-rule in January. More than 100,000 Arabs live in Hebron.
The city has been the scene of almost daily demonstrations along a confrontation line dividing Arab and Jewish areas in recent weeks.
